title: Completions Support Administrator
description:
Completions Support Administrator

Hybrid - Milton Keynes

About the Company

Our client is a UK-based Shariah-compliant challenger bank, founded in 2007, with offices in London, Milton Keynes, Birmingham and Wilmslow.

The organisation provides ethical savings products and residential property finance, alongside expertise in UK real estate investment.

Operating in accordance with Shariah principles, the business combines strong values with a modern, customer-focused approach, providing specialist financial solutions while maintaining a strong commitment to responsible and ethical practices.

The Role

Working closely with colleagues across the business, this role plays a key part in ensuring a seamless Home Finance customer journey.

You'll support applications from submission through to offer and completion, helping to drive an efficient, accurate and timely process at every stage.

What You'll Be Doing
- Take full ownership of post-offer applications, managing cases end-to-end to deliver positive outcomes for brokers and customers.
- Assess and process applications in line with Credit Policy, Customer Due Diligence (CDD) requirements and operational procedures.
- Contribute to an exceptional customer experience and consistently high service standards.
- Manage application pipelines effectively, progressing cases efficiently and in line with established processes, policies and agreed SLAs.
- Handle post-offer inbound and outbound telephone communications professionally and efficiently, consistently meeting agreed KPIs.
- Complete all pre-completion checks accurately and efficiently prior to the release of funds.
- Support the management of completion workflows, ensuring responses and actions are completed within agreed SLAs.
- Act as the main point of contact for external solicitors, facilitating the smooth and timely exchange of information and documentation.
- Work collaboratively with colleagues across the business to ensure applications progress smoothly through to completion.
- Maintain accurate records and ensure all activity is completed in accordance with regulatory and operational requirements.

What We're Looking For
- Experience within a Home Purchase Plan, mortgage, property finance or another financial services operational environment.
- Experience working within a process-driven environment where accuracy and attention to detail are essential.
- A passion for delivering excellent service and positive outcomes for customers.
- Strong organisational skills, with the ability to manage multiple applications and competing priorities.
- Excellent communication skills, with the confidence to liaise with customers, brokers, solicitors and internal stakeholders.
- The ability to work collaboratively within a dynamic and fast-paced team environment.
- A proactive approach, with the ability to take ownership of cases and see them through to completion.

Working Arrangements

This is an office-based role with hybrid working, offering flexibility to work from home for up to 3 days per week.

What You'll Get in Return

The successful candidate will receive a competitive and well-rounded benefits package, including:
- 25 days' holiday entitlement, increasing with service
- Pension plan
- Private medical insurance
- Dental cover
- Income protection
- Life assurance
- Employee referral bonus

The Curve Group is a Recruitment Services and Human Resources business with a mission to transform the working lives of the people and organisations we work with.

We collect and process your personal data for the purpose of providing recruitment and related HR services, in line with our legitimate business interests and legal obligations.
We will retain your data for two years from the last point of contact, after which it will be securely deleted unless you request otherwise.

For more details about how we handle your personal data and your rights, please see our full Privacy Policy on our website.

title: Finance Assistant
description:
We are recruiting for a Finance Assistant to join our team!

The Finance Assistant plays a key role in supporting the day-to-day financial operations of the business. There may be a focus on Accounts Payable or Credit Management activities, but the role will provide broader support across the Finance team as required. This is an excellent opportunity for an organised and detail-oriented individual looking to develop their finance career within a collaborative environment.

Please note this role is a 12-month fixed-term contract to support ongoing project work.

This is an exciting opportunity to work within our growing team in our new offices in Marlow! We will offer a work from home option (which is to be agreed directly with your line manager upon successful completion of your training).

As part of working for TTi, we offer many exciting benefits! It's our people that are crucial to the success of our business and therefore we offer a vast range of comprehensive benefits to our team.
- Free on-site parking at the office
- A non-contractual work from home option (ideally on successful completion of first 3 months of employment)
- 25 days holiday + bank holidays
- Private Medical & Dental Insurance
- Group Life Assurance Benefits
- Annual Gym Allowance
- Discounted Milwaukee, Ryobi and VAX products
- Access to our TTi Benefits Hub which includes discounts with many high street retailers
- Support towards Eye Sight Tests for DSE use
- On-site 3rd party restaurant and coffee shop in our offices

As well as the above benefits, the wellbeing of our employees is of utmost importance to us and we offer an Employee Assistance Programme, giving employees access to a confidential helpline 24/7.

Key Responsibilities may include:
- Process supplier invoices accurately and in a timely manner, ensuring compliance with company policies and financial controls.
- Reconcile supplier or customer statements ensuring queries are identified and resolved in an efficient manner.
- Set up of new supplier or customer accounts.
- Invoice matching to purchase orders raised in Basware (purchase to pay software).
- Purchase requisition/purchase order production.
- Process Adyen/PayPal payment files and reconcile to e-com ledger in a timely manner, ensuring compliance with company policies and financial controls.
- Process rebate and sales adjustment credit notes in a timely manner, ensuring compliance with company policies and financial controls.
- Support cash allocations as required.
- Oversee generic joint mailboxes to ensure that emails received are responded to/resolved in a timely and appropriate manner.
- Logging of customs paperwork and completion of declarations online.
- Carry out any other ad hoc responsibilities as required by your Line Manager.

Experience & Skills Required:
- Ideally 1-2 years' experience within a Finance Assistant/Accounts Assistant position.
- Strong numerical and analytical skills.
- Intermediate Microsoft Excel skills.
- Experience with SAP (highly desirable) and Basware would be an advantage.
- Strong stakeholder management and communication skills (both written and verbal as you will from time to time speak with suppliers on the phone).
- Ability to work to tight deadlines in a methodical, detailed and organised manner.
- Excellent accuracy and strong attention to detail is essential.
- Able to work well within a team environment but also with limited supervision.
- Confident to challenge the status quo to improve processes.
- Positive, proactive attitude with a willingness to learn.
- Adaptable and able to manage changing priorities.

title: Graduate Finance Assistant Accountant
description:
The Permanent Division of Robert Half is currently recruiting for a Graduate Finance Assistant Accountant role on behalf of a Sales business with offices in Milton Keynes

The Role

As Graduate Finance Assistant Accountant you will will be responsible for supporting the day-to-day management of the organisation's cash flow, banking operations, and treasury processes. This role ensures that all banking transactions are accurately processed, reconciled, and reported within in a timely manner. Day to day duties will consist of:
- Monitor daily cash balances and ensure adequate funding for operational requirements.
- Prepare and process electronic payments, bank transfers, and direct debits.
- Download and reconcile bank statements and credit card statements.
- Investigate discrepancies between the bank account and promptly.
- Maintain accurate records of cash movements, investments, and loan schedules.
- Assist in cash flow forecasting and provide regular treasury reports.
- Support month-end and year-end financial close processes relating to treasury activities.

Your Profile

You will be a Recent Graduate ideally with a Mathematics, Economics or Accounting based Degree or a College Leaver having studied a similar course or AAT. You will have an interest in finance and numbers with strong numerical and analytical skills and excellent attention to detail. Previous experience with Microsoft Excel is highly preferred. This is an excellent first finance role which will be well supported and in a successful organisation.

Salary and Benefits

Role of Graduate Finance Assistant Accountant is a Permanent Opportunity and working 5 days a week in the office in Milton Keynes. The role is paying up to £26 K + Study + Benefits

title: Medical Events Project Co-ordinator
company: Bucks and Berks Recruitment - Agency - Permanent
description:
Are you an organised and proactive project professional with a passion for delivering high-quality events and educational programmes?

Our client, a leading medical education and media publishing organisation, is looking to recruit a Medical Events Project Coordinator to join their collaborative Projects Team.

This is an exciting opportunity to work on a variety of virtual and face-to-face educational programmes, partnering with leading physicians, global healthcare organisations and internal specialist teams to deliver engaging, impactful content.

As a Medical Events Project Coordinator, you will support the delivery of client-funded educational programmes from initial planning through to publication. You'll coordinate multiple projects simultaneously, ensuring activities are delivered on time, within budget and to the highest quality standards.

The role is hybrid (2 days in the office, 3 from home) and comes with excellent benefits.

Key responsibilities include:
- Coordinating virtual and live educational events, including webinars, interviews, round tables, peer-to-peer discussions and symposia.
- Managing project timelines, schedules and deliverables throughout the project lifecycle.
- Liaising with leading physicians, key opinion leaders and industry stakeholders.
- Working closely with internal teams including Account Management, Marketing, Medical Writing, Education and Digital Media.
- Supporting client communications and providing regular project updates.
- Coordinating filming sessions, content creation activities and event logistics.
- Ensuring projects meet agreed objectives, budgets and deadlines.
- Maintaining accurate project documentation and adhering to established processes.

Skills/Experience
- A minimum of two years' experience working as an Events Coordinator / Associate Project Manager/events professional, ideally with a medical communications, events, publishing or agency background.
- First-class non-technical project management skills with a proven track record of delivering a number of projects of varying complexity across the health education sector.
- Qualified to degree level or equivalent. A science-based subject is desirable (although not essential).
- Adept at developing effective relationships with internal and external stakeholders.
- Strong communication and inter-personal skills.
- The ability to multi-task and work on several complex client projects simultaneously.
- The ability to prioritise a heavy workload and work to tight deadlines.
- Self-motivated and able to work without detailed supervision.

Please note that we will only contact those candidates that we assess as suitable for the positions we have currently available based on their experience, training, and skills. If we do not have anything suitable, we will not keep your CV for more than 30 days.

title: Receptionist
description: We are looking for a Receptionist/Administrator to join our friendly and supportive team at Purbeck Health Centre. This is an important front-line role where you will help patients access the right care while supporting the smooth day-to-day running of the practice. Friendly, approachable and professional Reliable, organised and able to manage competing priorities Confident communicating with patients and colleagues Comfortable using computers and learning new systems Able to work independently and as part of a team Committed to providing excellent patient service Previous experience in a GP practice or healthcare setting would be helpful, but it is not essential. Full training will be provided, and you will be supported by an experienced team who take pride in delivering excellent care and service to our patients. If you are looking for a rewarding and varied role where you can make a real difference to patients every day, we would love to hear from you. What you will be doing Answering telephone calls and responding to patient enquiries Welcoming patients at the reception desk Booking and managing appointments Completing a variety of administrative tasks Working closely with our clinical and administrative teams Handling confidential information professionally The role is busy and varied, so you will need excellent communication and organisational skills, good attention to detail, and the ability to remain calm under pressure. Job Description Job title: Receptionist/Administrator Location: Purbeck Health Centre, Milton Keynes Hours: Working pattern to be agreed Reports to: Reception Lead/Practice Manager The Receptionist/Administrator will be one of the first points of contact for patients and visitors. The postholder will provide a professional and welcoming reception service, manage telephone calls and patient enquiries, and complete a range of computer-based administrative duties. The role is essential to supporting the smooth day-to-day running of the practice and ensuring patients receive a helpful, efficient and respectful service. Welcome patients and visitors in a friendly, caring and professional manner. Check patients in for appointments and assist with general enquiries. Support the smooth flow of patients through the practice. Communicate with clinicians and other team members when required. Keep the reception area calm, tidy and organised. Respect patients privacy and maintain confidentiality at all times. Answer incoming telephone calls promptly and courteously. Book, amend and cancel appointments accurately using SystmOne. Respond to general enquiries and direct patients to the appropriate service or member of staff. Follow practice procedures when receiving urgent or emergency calls and escalate concerns immediately where required. Take clear and accurate messages and pass them to the appropriate clinician or administrator promptly. Communicate sensitively with patients who may be worried, distressed or frustrated. Update patient contact details, appointment information and records accurately. Process online appointment requests, messages and administrative queries. Maintain accurate patient records, tasks and worklists on SystmOne. Monitor emails, call queues and other practice communication systems. Support the smooth running of the days appointments and reception services. Complete general administrative duties, including printing letters, preparing lists and entering data. Follow practice procedures for filing, communication and information sharing. Work closely with reception colleagues to maintain appropriate cover for the front desk and telephone lines. Communicate clearly and professionally with clinicians, administrators and management. Provide additional cover during colleagues annual leave or sickness where required. Attend team meetings, training sessions and practice updates. Contribute ideas that could improve patient services or working processes. Promote a positive, respectful and supportive working environment. Follow all practice policies and procedures, including those relating to confidentiality, safeguarding, information governance and data protection. Maintain a professional, respectful and positive approach. Report incidents, risks or concerns promptly to the Reception Lead or Practice Manager. Complete all required mandatory training. Keep knowledge of practice systems, policies and procedures up to date. Work within the responsibilities and boundaries of the role. Excellent communication and telephone skills. A friendly, polite and approachable manner. Confidence using computers and learning new systems. Good organisational skills and the ability to manage competing priorities. Ability to remain calm and professional in a busy environment. Strong attention to detail and accuracy. A reliable, flexible and supportive approach to teamwork. Understanding of the importance of patient confidentiality. Commitment to providing a high standard of patient service. Previous experience in a GP practice, healthcare setting or customer-facing role. Experience using SystmOne or another clinical record system. The postholder must promote equality, diversity and inclusion and treat all patients, visitors and colleagues with dignity, fairness and respect. The postholder must take reasonable care of their own health and safety and that of others who may be affected by their work. Any hazards, incidents or concerns must be reported promptly in accordance with practice procedures. All patient, staff and practice information must be treated as confidential. The postholder must follow UK GDPR, data protection requirements, NHS information governance standards and practice policies. The postholder will be expected to: Uphold the values and reputation of Purbeck Health Centre. Follow all practice policies, procedures and applicable NHS requirements. Take responsibility for their own learning, training and professional development. Contribute to a positive, supportive and inclusive workplace. Carry out other reasonable duties appropriate to the role. This job description provides an overview of the role and is not exhaustive. Duties may change as the needs of the practice develop, following appropriate discussion with the postholder and their line manager.

Receive referrals into the service and allocate work to teams and individual clinical staff using agreed allocation tools, policies and procedures. Book, manage and amend appointments for service lines in line with local policies and processes, maintaining accurate electronic and paper records as required. Information handled may be confidential and of a sensitive nature. Respond to queries both face-to-face and via telephone, ensuring messages are accurately recorded and passed to the appropriate member of staff in a timely manner. Create, update and maintain clinical records in accordance with Information Governance requirements, Trust policies and clinical system guidance. Enter and maintain clinical and demographic data on Trust systems accurately and promptly, including appointments, referrals, attendance records and other service-related information. Support clinical staff within clinic settings, ensuring attendance registers and patient records are updated and maintained appropriately. Produce information packs, correspondence and other documentation required by service lines. Undertake general administrative duties including copy typing, scanning, photocopying, printing, filing and document management. Manage incoming and outgoing post, emails and other communications on a daily basis. Make and receive telephone calls to both internal and external stakeholders as required by the service. Assist with meeting arrangements, preparation of documentation and coordination of information as required. Organise and maintain inventories of office and clinical equipment and support associated calibration processes where necessary. Attend and actively participate in team meetings, service meetings, supervision sessions, appraisals and regular reviews with line management. Prepare for and participate in assessments, training programmes and development activities as required by the Trust. Support the induction, demonstration of processes and training of staff within the remit of the role. Work in accordance with Milton Keynes safeguarding policies, procedures and codes of practice. Maintain awareness and understanding of infection prevention and control requirements relating to adults, children and young people. Maintain strict confidentiality at all times and comply with all relevant data protection and information governance requirements. Present a professional manner and appearance at all times when representing the service and Trust. Act as a flexible and supportive member of the team, providing cover and assistance across services as required. Undertake any other duties commensurate with the grade of the post to meet the operational needs of the service and Trust.
